description: Every number, name and enum an Asgard implementation would otherwise copy out of protocol.md, each with the section it comes from. Where the spec gives a level, `level` is MUST, SHOULD, RECOMMENDED or MAY; `default` marks a value the spec calls sensible or that the reference implementations use, which an implementation may change.

protocol.note: The integer in `protocol` in every body, and the value of the Asgard-Protocol header as a string. A client supports exactly one version per build; a server MAY support several.

encodings.note: Values of `accepts` in the handshake and `encoding` in its answer.

base.note: {base} is an https: URL with no query, no fragment and no trailing slash. A development build MAY accept http:; a production build MUST NOT.

list.name: session
list.used_for: The handshake. Always a plain POST, never with X-Asgard-Method.

list.name: render
list.used_for: Region requests, batches, server screens and actions.

list.name: stream
list.used_for: The push stream. The request is sealed; the answer's headers are not, and each event is sealed on its own.

list.name: upload
list.used_for: Uploads. The decrypted body is a frame, not JSON.

safe_requests.note: Only these may probe the transport as QUERY. Until the probe settles, every other request goes as POST plus X-Asgard-Method: QUERY.

fallback_on_status.note: Or any answer that is not a valid Asgard answer, on the first safe request after a handshake.

headers.name: Asgard-Session-Id
headers.note: On every request after the handshake. Its value is the session id, which is also the signature keyid and the aes128gcm keyid.

headers.name: Asgard-Protocol
headers.note: A covered component of every signed request and response. The spec covers it but never states its value; the reference implementations send "1".

headers.name: X-Asgard-Method
headers.note: Turns a POST into a QUERY. Never on {base}/session.

headers.name: Authorization
headers.note: The app's own bearer token. Covered when, and only when, the request carries it.

headers.name: Content-Type
headers.note: A client MUST send it. It stays application/json for encrypted bodies and upload frames. A stream answer is text/event-stream.

headers.name: Content-Encoding
headers.note: Always aes128gcm on a sealed message. A server MUST refuse a request with any other coding.

headers.name: Content-Digest
headers.note: sha-256 over the body as sent (the ciphertext).

headers.name: Asgard-Content-Coding
headers.note: On every sealed response. Any other value, or no header, MUST be refused.

headers.name: Asgard-Cache
headers.note: One lowercase word of up to 32 letters. A client ignores any value but invalidate. Unsigned answers never carry it.

headers.name: Signature-Input
headers.note: RFC 9421. The Asgard member is labelled asgard.

headers.name: Signature
headers.note: RFC 9421. The Asgard member is labelled asgard.

headers.name: Last-Event-ID
headers.note: Sent on a stream reconnect. Not signed, and a server MUST ignore it: version tokens decide what is sent on connect.

statuses.name: No Content
statuses.used_for: Ending a push stream. The client MUST NOT reconnect until the set changes.

statuses.name: Unauthorized
statuses.used_for: The app's bearer token was rejected. The body is the app's. Handed to the app's auth flow.

statuses.name: Forbidden
statuses.used_for: A failed check, a reused or missing nonce, or an unknown key at the handshake. The client MUST NOT retry.

statuses.name: Not Found
statuses.used_for: An unknown address, region, action or method.

statuses.name: Method Not Allowed
statuses.used_for: A method the endpoint does not accept.

statuses.name: Content Too Large
statuses.used_for: An upload over its size limit.

statuses.name: Unsupported Media Type
statuses.used_for: An upload of a type the method does not accept.
The session is missing, unknown or expired. The client re-handshakes once and retries once. Not a registered code (open question 12).

statuses.name: Unprocessable Content
statuses.used_for: A body that is well formed but wrong.

statuses.name: Internal Server Error
statuses.used_for: A fragment or delta the server could not produce.

statuses.name: Not Implemented
statuses.used_for: Sent by something in front of the server that refuses QUERY. The client falls back to POST.

errors.meaning: The handshake named a key the server does not know, or the server has none configured.
The server does not speak the client's protocol. The body also carries `protocols`, the list it does speak.
No encoding in `accepts` is one the server speaks.
On session anything but POST; elsewhere anything but QUERY or POST with X-Asgard-Method: QUERY.
Over the method's limit or the server's. Plain and unsigned when the server can tell from the size alone, before decrypting; sealed otherwise.
Asgard-Session-Id is missing, unknown or expired.
The digest, the signature or its freshness, a reused nonce, or decryption failed.

errors.sealed: call and upload: plain; render action: sealed
errors.meaning: An action, method call or upload whose signature has no nonce. A call or upload is refused before decrypting; an action is only found after.
An unknown address, or a well-formed region name the component does not have, wherever a request names one: a render or batch, an action, a call's or upload's regions, or a stream subscription.
`action.call` is not a method the component exposed to clients.
Not a method the component exposed for calls (or, on upload, for uploads).
The type sniffed from the file's bytes is not one the method accepts.

A malformed body, a malformed regions list or region name, a malformed read_only or cache, a bad reason, an action that does not name exactly one region, a stream request with an action or a bad subscription, an unknown member where one is refused, state or args that do not fit, or a bad upload frame.
The request, or one stream subscription, names more regions than the server's limit. Nothing is rendered or streamed, and a call's method does not run.
A delta value is not a plain JSON value.
In development, the server changed a member the request named in read_only. In production it leaves the member out and logs it.
A fragment the server cannot send, such as one using a type the client did not advertise. Named only in §8.1; the other endpoints follow the general 500 rule.

early_rejections.note: The only unsigned answers after the handshake. A client acts on their status only, and checks the body against this list only while it probes the transport.

check_order.note: A request that fails any of the first five MUST be discarded before anything parses its body, and those five MUST run ahead of the server's own request handling.

failure_reasons.meaning: The request never reached the server, or nothing came back.
The server answered with an error, including a 419 after its one retry.
The answer failed verification, or its fragment cannot be rendered.
Uploads only: the file cannot be read as a regular local file. Nothing was sent.
Uploads only: the file is over the client's own limit. Nothing was sent.

request.optional_note: Covered after the rest, in this order, when and only when the request carries them.
request.authority: the host in lowercase, with the port when it is not the scheme's default
request.path: the path as sent, without the query

response.optional_note: asgard-cache is covered right after asgard-protocol and before "signature";req;key="asgard", when and only when the response carries it.

lines: <the stream request's 32-byte signature, base64 with padding>

handshake.point_encoding: uncompressed, 0x04 || X || Y (SEC 1 §2.3.3), base64url without padding
handshake.info: "asgard/1 session" || 0x00 || client_public || server_public (the 65 raw bytes of each)

ephemeral.note: Each side makes a key pair for one handshake and discards the private key once the secret is derived.

list.name: sig_s
list.used_for: HMAC signing of responses and events

list.name: enc_s
list.used_for: aes128gcm IKM for response bodies and event bodies

content_encoding.name: aes128gcm

salt_bytes.note: Fresh and random for every message and every event.

content_encoding.keyid: the session id; a receiver MUST refuse any other

nonce.remembered: per session, until its expires plus the clock skew allowance

gzip.header_note: Fixed header: no file name, mtime 0, OS 255. The header and level are fixed so answers are comparable, not byte-identical: deflate builds differ, so a receiver checks a compressed body by inflating it, never by comparing bytes.

min_plaintext_bytes.note: Below this a region answer or event is not compressed.

inflate_cap_bytes.note: 8 MiB. A client gives up as soon as inflated output passes it.

compressible: region answers (render, batch, screen, action) with delta {} where every region allows it

clock_skew_future_seconds.note: A request's created may be up to this far in the future.

request_lifetime_max_seconds.note: expires is at most this long after created. A request past its expires MUST be refused.

response_created_ahead_max_seconds.note: A client refuses a response whose created is further ahead of its clock.

response_created_behind_max_seconds.note: A client refuses a response whose created is further behind its clock.

session_early_expiry_seconds.note: A client treats a session as gone this long before expires_in says it lapses.

region_timeout_seconds.note: 0 means no limit (MAY, set per component).

action_timeout_seconds.note: Also applies to chrome actions and method calls. 0 means no limit.

screen_timeout_seconds.note: How long a server screen waits for its first body.

stream_backoff_max_seconds.note: Reconnect backoff: the server's retry, doubled per failure in a row, at most this.

stream_lifetime_seconds.note: How long a server keeps a stream open. A sensible default; unrelated to the signature window.

route_retry_seconds.note: A failed route list fetch may be retried a minute later.

cache_fresh_skew_seconds.note: A declared copy is fresh when the time since made_at by the server's clock is at least this.

cache_renew_margin_seconds.note: A server SHOULD render a copy with little time left; 30 seconds is a sensible default.

patch_record_wait_ms.note: What the reference server waits for the record of the newest patch step (MAY), and at least one poll.

region_name.note: A name that does not match is 422 invalid_request; a well-formed name the component does not have is 404 unknown_component.

regions_per_request.note: A server SHOULD set its own limit and answer a request over it with 422 too_many_regions. The same limit applies to a call's or upload's regions and to each stream subscription. The reference implementations allow 16.

action_regions.note: A request with an action names exactly one region.

redraw_parts.note: 16 inline regions plus the action's own.

subscription_regions.note: No fixed maximum: each subscription is held to the server's limit on regions per request (§3.1), with 422 too_many_regions.

upload_header_bytes.note: 1 MiB. The frame's uint32 length prefix is big-endian.

route_segment.note: Literal segments; parameters are {name}, with an optional {name?} allowed last.

font_weight.note: A client clamps other values into the range.

read_only.note: A list of distinct strings, each a member of state. Any other shape is 422 invalid_request.

compare_and_set.note: The client applies each delta member only if it still holds the value it sent.

route_value_booleans.note: A server converts a numeric string to a number and these strings to booleans, and nothing else.

reasons.note: The only value of `reason`, on a render request sent because of a push. Any other value is 422 invalid_request; a call or upload MUST NOT carry it.

unknown_members_refused_in.note: Everywhere else a receiver ignores a member it does not know.
